[[File:Location map Indonesia Aceh.png|thumb|Location map Indonesia Aceh]]

'''Rudi Putra''' is an Indonesian [[biologist]] who received a [[Goldman Environmental Prize]] in 2014 for his efforts to combat illegal logging, forest encroachment for [[palm oil production]], and policies that open endangered ecosystems to mining and plantation [[industry (economics)|industries]].<ref name="satu">{{cite web|url=http://news.mongabay.com/2014/0428-goldman-prize-rudi-putra.html|title=Indonesian activist wins Goldman Prize for fighting palm oil, deforestation|accessdate=14 May 2014|work=news.mongabay.com}}</ref>

[[File:Elaeis guineensis MS 3467.jpg|thumb|[[Elaeis|Oil palm]]]]
Putra is a biologist who worked in Aceh Province, and who received a prize of $175,000 from his winning of the Goldman Environmental Prize in 2014.<ref name="satu"/> Putra was selected as the winner in the category 'Island and Island Nations'.<ref name="satu"/> He was recognized for his campaign to reclaim the land under illegal palm oil plantations in the Leuser Ecosystem, Sumatra, and to clear them in order to re-establish habitat for endangered [[orangutans]], [[tigers]], rhinoceros, and [[elephants]], as well as lobbying against political plans to remove protected status from Aceh's primary forests.<ref name="dua">{{cite web|url=http://www.radioaustralia.net.au/indonesian/2014-04-29/selamatkan-badak-sumatera-rudi-putra-terima-goldman-prize/1302440|title=Selamatkan Badak Sumatera, Rudi Putra Terima Goldman Prize|accessdate=14 May 2014|work=radioaustralia.net.au}}</ref> In 2013, these activities culminated in the establishment of a petition that asked the Indonesian government to enforce [[conservation law]] and reject the proposals in Aceh.<ref name="dua"/> The petition received more than 1.4 million signatures, increasing awareness of [[environmental issues in Indonesia]] and attracting widespread international condemnation.<ref name="dua"/>
[[File:Sumatraanse Tijger.jpg|thumb|Sumatran Tiger]]

==Motivation==
As a high school student who grew up in the region of Aceh, Putra showed a keen interest in the natural world.<ref name="tiga">{{cite web|url=http://www.goldmanprize.org/recipient/rudi-putra|title=Rudi Putra, 2014 Islands & Island Nations|accessdate=14 May 2014|work=goldmanprize.org}}</ref> He studied the biology and [[Wildlife conservation|conservation]] of the Sumatran rhino: the smallest member of the most endangered rhinoceros in the family.<ref name="tiga"/>

Putra become an expert researcher and also a tracker, who led an expedition aiming to protects [[rhinoceros]] in the field by pursuing and catching poachers in the Leuser Ecosystem.<ref name="tiga"/> The area, which has an area of 6.4 million hectares of forest stretching from Aceh to [[North Sumatra]], is federally protected and is one of the largest remaining habitats supporting the Sumatran rhino.<ref name="tiga"/>

Putra realised that in addition to attempting to stop illegal hunting, his efforts would not be complete without discussing and confronting the threat posed by habitat destruction from illegal logging and palm oil plantations.<ref name="tiga"/> Further studies show the importance of forests for the 4 million people living close to the Leuser Ecosystem.<ref name="tiga"/> Forests also provide protection from flooding; in the Leuser ecosystem the frequency and severity has been increasing.<ref name="tiga"/> Putra sees it as his job not only to protect the rhinos and their habitat, but also the people of the region.<ref name="tiga"/>

==Illegal palm oil plantations==
[[File:Bospad te Atjeh.jpg|thumb|upright|Forest path in Atjeh]]

In the course of rescuing the land from the 'oilers' and enabling the natural ecosystems to regain their hold, Putra's approach was soundly based on grassroots innovations rather than direct lobbying of local government.<ref name="keempat">{{cite web|url=http://inhabitat.com/environmental-hero-rudi-putra-wins-2014-green-nobel-goldman-prize/rudi-putra-in-a-restored-section-of-the-leuser-ecosystem-indonesia/?extend=1|title=Environmental Hero Rudi Putra Wins 2014 "Green Nobel" Goldman|accessdate=14 May 2014|work=inhabitat.com}}</ref><ref name="kelima">{{cite web|url=http://greentv.com/renewables/environmental-hero-rudi-putra-wins-2014-green-nobel-goldman-prize/|title=Environmental Hero Rudi Putra Wins 2014 "Green Nobel" Goldman|accessdate=14 May 2014|work=greentv.com|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20140504171923/http://greentv.com/renewables/environmental-hero-rudi-putra-wins-2014-green-nobel-goldman-prize/|archivedate=4 May 2014}}</ref> This approach involved supporting a programme of local community education about the problem and how the scale of [[illegal logging]] threatens the lives not only of [[animals]] but also the people of [[Aceh]].<ref name="keempat"/> Putra created a chain of support from members of the community which started and gradually increased to include members of the government and police service.<ref name="keempat"/> Currently, Putra oversees the recovery team that cut down the forest of palm trees in the [[Leuser Ecosystem]].<ref name="keempat"/> To this day, Putra has managed to reduce 26 illegal [[Elaeis|oil palm plantations]]. Twenty-four of these were closed willingly by the owners, whilst the other two were forcibly closed after a [[police]] operation following legal action.<ref name="keempat"/>

== FKL ==
Rudi and his colleagues founded Forum Konservasi Leuser (FKL) in 2013, which operates 28 teams to protect the leuser ecosystem by dismantling snares and restoring damaged forest. Most of the forest is restored naturally rather than through tree planting. Some 5,000 ha have been restored in this way as of 2021.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Hanafiah |first=Juinaidi |date=June 17, 2021 |title=Never too late to save Earth: Q&A with Leuser forest guardian Rudi Putra |url=https://news.mongabay.com/2021/06/never-too-late-to-save-earth-qa-with-leuser-forest-guardian-rudi-putra/ |access-date=November 19, 2023 |website=Mongabay}}</ref>

==Awards==
[[Environmental activists]] from six regions of the world received an award as part of the Goldman Environmental Prize in [[San Francisco]] on 28 April 2014.<ref name="keenam">{{cite web|url=https://www.voanews.com/a/grassroots-activists-awarded-goldman-environmental-prize-/1901286.html|title=Grassroots Activists Awarded Goldman Environmental Prize|access-date=4 May 2014|work=Voice of America}}</ref> Each year the award is worth a $175,000 award for the individuals who have shown huge courage and initiative against the odds to take action to protect their [[Natural environment|environment]].<ref name="keenam"/>

The six winners in 2014 were [[Desmond D'Sa]] is from [[South Africa]], [[Suren Gazaryan]] from [[Russia]], [[Ramesh Agrawal]] from [[India]], [[Ruth Buendia]] from [[Peru]], [[Helen Slottje]] from [[United States|America]], and Putra Son representing [[Indonesia]].<ref name="keenam"/>

In 2013 Rudy won the [[Future For Nature Award]], worth €50,000 for individuals passionate about nature conservation.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://futurefornature.org/winners/rudi-putra/|title=Rudi Putra|date=20 August 2018|website=Future For Nature}}</ref>
